rules.label: Hamza break
rules.explanation: Contains a glottal stop that is often skipped outside Arabic.

rules.label: Pinyin x
rules.explanation: Pinyin x is often read like English x by non-Chinese speakers.

rules.label: Czech ř
rules.explanation: The ř sound is distinctive and often hard for non-Czech speakers.

rules.label: Soft Danish sounds
rules.explanation: Soft Danish vowels and consonants often invite wrong guesses.

rules.label: Dutch ij
rules.explanation: IJ has a Dutch reading that many visitors do not guess correctly.

rules.label: Silent letters
rules.explanation: Contains a gh sequence that English speakers often guess wrong.

rules.label: Uncommon letter combination
rules.explanation: Contains a Gaelic-style consonant blend that many readers will not parse correctly.

rules.label: Ambiguous vowel cluster
rules.explanation: Two-vowel cluster with multiple likely readings.

rules.label: Ambiguous vowel cluster
rules.explanation: EIGH patterns produce multiple English guesses.

rules.label: Uncommon letter combination
rules.explanation: SZ is uncommon in English-first names and often causes hesitation.

rules.label: Uncommon letter frequency
rules.explanation: X in the middle of a given name increases dictation friction.

rules.label: Finnish front vowel
rules.explanation: Ö needs a Finnish-style vowel reading to sound natural.

rules.label: French vowel cluster
rules.explanation: EAU is easy to misread when guessed from spelling alone.

rules.label: German sch
rules.explanation: SCH is stable in German but often read differently by visitors.

rules.label: Greek nasal cluster
rules.explanation: This Greek cluster is often not pronounced as written by non-Greek speakers.

rules.label: Hebrew het
rules.explanation: The het sound is often flattened by readers outside Hebrew.

rules.label: Hindi conjunct
rules.explanation: This consonant conjunct is commonly misread by non-Hindi speakers.

rules.label: Indonesian kh
rules.explanation: KH may be pronounced too literally by readers outside Indonesian.

rules.label: Italian gli
rules.explanation: GLI has a specific Italian reading that is easy to miss.

rules.label: Small kana glide
rules.explanation: Small kana modify the previous sound and are often skipped by learners.

rules.label: Korean rieul
rules.explanation: This Korean consonant moves between r and l readings depending on position.

rules.label: Norwegian kj
rules.explanation: KJ has a local reading that is often guessed incorrectly.

rules.label: Polish sz
rules.explanation: SZ is readable in Polish but often misread by outsiders.

rules.label: Nasal vowel
rules.explanation: The nasal ão ending is often hard to reproduce outside Portuguese.

rules.label: Letter ё
rules.explanation: Ё is often written as Е, which can cause the wrong reading.

rules.label: Russian щ
rules.explanation: Щ is frequently simplified or confused by non-Russian speakers.

rules.label: Spanish ll
rules.explanation: LL has region-dependent readings that can cause pronunciation drift.

rules.label: Swedish sj
rules.explanation: SJ is one of the harder Swedish consonant clusters for visitors.

rules.label: Thai vocalic rue
rules.explanation: This Thai character has a reading that many learners do not infer from shape.

rules.label: Turkish soft g
rules.explanation: Ğ lengthens or softens the surrounding vowels and is often pronounced too hard.

rules.label: Ukrainian ї
rules.explanation: Ї has a Ukrainian-specific reading that is often flattened by visitors.

rules.label: Vietnamese ng
rules.explanation: NG at the start of a name often causes hesitation for non-Vietnamese speakers.
